From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood deployment options — SSO / KMS / log retention follow-up

Aisha — thanks, this is exactly the kind of detail we needed. Quick answers and notes below; happy to expand on the technical call.

SSO / SCIM
- Confirmed: we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for user and service accounts. We can configure automatic deprovisioning with Okta.

KMS / HSM
- Summary: 
  - Hosted API: does not support customer-managed KMS keys or HSM integration (hosted keys only).
  - Dedicated capacity: supports BYOK via AWS KMS CMKs in your account (we can configure encryption-at-rest to use a CMK you control if the Dedicated stack is deployed in your cloud account/region).
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): supports full HSM integrations (CloudHSM and customer HSM appliances) and gives you the widest control over key material and key lifecycle.
- From your note it sounds like a hybrid requirement: BYOK via AWS KMS is fine for most traffic, but high-risk flows requiring HSM will push us toward Private. We'll cover options for splitting workloads (routing high-risk traffic to Private) on the call.

Logs & retention
- Hosted API: standard retention (30–90 days) and org-level export only — not suitable for 7-year retention.
- Dedicated: can extend retention windows and support exporting logs to a customer S3 bucket under a cross-account role; retention policies can be configured up to multi-year but long-term archival typically needs Private for full control.
- Private: you control log retention, can archive directly to your S3 in us-west-2, and we can set up secure streaming to Splunk (via HEC or an event push).

Data residency
- We can provision Dedicated or Private in us-west-2. Hosted API for production traffic would not guarantee dedicated residency.

Recommendations
- Given your HSM requirement for some production flows and 7-year retention, Private (VPC or on-prem) is likely the safest fit. However, if you want a phased approach, we can start with Dedicated for early traffic (BYOK via AWS KMS) and migrate the high-risk flows to Private later.

Next steps
1) Tech call (60 min): Rishi (security), Dylan (solutions) + your infra/security engineers. Proposed: Wed 12/16 10:00 PT — works for us. I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.
2) I’ll attach a short matrix that maps SSO/KMS/log capabilities to each deployment option to make the decision easier.
3) If helpful, we can prepare a scoped runbook for migrating specific workloads from Dedicated -> Private.

Thanks — cc'ing Rishi and Dylan to confirm.

Best,
